title: Jesus and the ‘prostitute.’ part 1
scripture_text: ‘’When one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to have dinner with him, he went to the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table. A woman in that town who lived a sinful life learned that Jesus was eating at the Pharisee’s house, so she came there with an alabaster jar of perfume. As she stood behind him at his feet weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears. Then she wiped them with her hair, kissed them and poured perfume on them. When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, he would know who is touching him and what kind of woman she is—that she is a sinner.” Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” “Tell me, teacher,” he said. “Two people owed money to a certain moneylender. One owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty. Neither of them had the money to pay him back, so he forgave the debts of both. Now which of them will love him more?” Simon replied, “I suppose the one who had the bigger debt forgiven.” “You have judged correctly,” Jesus said. Then he turned toward the woman and said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I came into your house. You did not give me any water for my feet, but she wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. You did not give me a kiss, but this woman, from the time I entered, has not stopped kissing my feet. You did not put oil on my head, but she has poured perfume on my feet. Therefore, I tell you, her many sins have been forgiven—as her great love has shown. But whoever has been forgiven little loves little. Then Jesus said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.” The other guests began to say among themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?” Jesus said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
devotional:
I want to start by asking this question, ‘How radical is our experience of Jesus?’ This is a very important question.

Has Jesus totally transformed your life or has he merely cleaned it up? In the book Emotional Healthy Disciples, Peter Scazzero writes,

“An emotionally healthy disciple slows down to be with Jesus, goes beneath the surface of their life to be deeply transformed by Jesus, and offers their life as a gift to the world for Jesus.” Peter Scazzero, Emotionally Healthy Discipleship: Moving from Shallow Christianity to Deep Transformation (Grand Rapids, MI: Zondervan, 2021).

We have imbibed a version of Christianity that is more about going to heaven than it is about profound transformation. Jesus does not want to clean us up and make us ‘nice.’ He wants to make us different, as new, radical disciples that unsettle the world where he has placed us. However, if we’re being honest, we do not want a radical Jesus to come and mess up our lives. We are content with a ‘tidy up,’ a ‘spring clean,’ when what we really need is a life reforming make over, we are happy with superficial, shallow obedience and fellowship with God that is neither costly or changing.

If our experience of Jesus does not make a tangible, lasting transforming difference to our lives then we may not be following the Jesus of the bible!!!

The story we are going to consider is a very well known story, and because it is so well known it has been sanitised, dumbed down to fit into our neat boxes. It is a story about a prostitute and a Pharisee. It is a story that should disturb and make us uncomfortable because the point of this story is, we need to become like this prostitute and not like this Pharisee.

The Context of the story

Luke tells us in 7:36 ‘One of the Pharisees asked Jesus to have dinner with him,’ we know from verse 40 that this Pharisee was called Simon. In Luke's gospel we read of Jesus being at 7 meals, Three of these meals were at the homes of Pharisees, Luke 7:36, 11:37, 14:1, these three meals were all contentious. We are not specifically told why Simon invited Jesus. But Luke gives us some clues.

1. Up to this point Luke has mentioned the Pharisees six time, 5:17,21,30, 33. 6:2,7 each time they are antagonistic against Jesus.

2.The way 7:36 is written in the Greek it reads ‘One of the Pharisees kept on asking.’ It gives the impression that Jesus may have known that this was a set up, and he did not just accept right away.

3. We are told that they were reclining at the table this would indicate that this was a formal or ceremonious occasion and yet we are told in verses 43-46 that Simon did not offer Jesus the customary expressions of welcome or acceptance. While not mandatory, it would have been a kind gesture for Simon as the host to have had his servants wash the feet of his guest. A kiss was a common form of greeting, although not necessary, it was an expected act of courtesy. It was also a kind gesture to anoint the head of one’s guest with olive oil.

It appears that Simon’s intention was to judge and critique, with the hope of finding fault.

Simon was discourteous and showed no affection to Jesus. He wanted a relationship with Jesus devoid of depth and meaning. This was a religious man who was unable to relate or connect meaningfully with Jesus. He did not want Jesus to make any demands upon him, He did not want Him to bring change or transformation into his life, he did not want Jesus to challenge his beliefs or lifestyle. Einstein once said, ‘School has ruined my education.’ Many Christians could say, ‘religion has ruined my relationship with Jesus.’ I think it should be the other way round. ‘Thankfully, Jesus has ruined my religion.’
prayer: Father may I experience your radical transformation in my life.
